## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by strongly curved, crescent-shaped cells with broadly rounded tips and a slightly swollen central region. Closterium moniliferum contains large chloroplasts with rows of pyrenoids and terminal vacuoles containing conspicuous moving crystalline granules. It occurs in freshwater habitats such as ponds, shallow lake margins, wetlands, and sediments, particularly in moderately nutrient-rich waters ranging from slightly acidic to alkaline conditions. Like other desmids, it contributes to primary production in freshwater ecosystems and forms part of the microscopic food web supporting aquatic invertebrates and other organisms.
